scenes.line1: How do trees and heaps power search?
scenes.say: Trees and heaps are everywhere in search, sorting, and priority tasks. Why are they so popular in interviews?

scenes.label: Trees
scenes.sub: Binary search trees order nodes; heaps use min or max rules.
scenes.say: A tree is a hierarchy. In binary search trees, nodes are ordered. Heaps are binary trees with min or max properties.
Traversals include breadth-first, which uses a queue, and depth-first, with pre, in, and post order. Balanced trees like AVL and Red-Black keep operations fast.

scenes.code:
import heapq
heapq.heapify(arr)
heapq.heappush(arr, val)
heapq.heappop(arr)
scenes.say: In Python, heapq lets you heapify, push, and pop efficiently. This is key for priority queues.

scenes.question: Is every binary tree balanced?
scenes.wrong: Yes, all binary trees are balanced.
scenes.right: No. Only AVL and Red-Black trees guarantee balance for O(log n) operations.
scenes.say: Here’s a trap: Not all binary trees are balanced. Only AVL and Red-Black trees guarantee fast operations.
